introduction_markdown: General Certificate of Education (GCE) Board, Ordinary Level, June 2025. Additional Mathematics, Paper 2 (code 0575). Time allowed: two and a half hours. Answer ALL questions in SECTION A (Pure Mathematics, compulsory) and ANY TWO questions from EITHER SECTION B (Mechanics) OR SECTION C (Statistics and Probability). In Sections B and C, all questions carry equal marks. Candidates are expected to answer a combination of Section A and Section B OR Section A and Section C, but NOT a combination of all three. If Section B is chosen, Section C may not be chosen, and the other way round. All necessary working must be shown. No marks will be awarded for answers without brief statements showing how the answers have been obtained. Non-programmable electronic calculators and Mathematical Formulae booklets published by the GCE Board are allowed. Where necessary take g as 10 m s^-2.

Points : le sujet imprime des points par sous-question, sans total par question. Le champ points de l'exercice est la somme des points imprimes des sous-questions.

9(iii)(a) : le diagramme des forces est a dessiner par le candidat ; le corrige le decrit (forces sur P : poids, reaction, tension ; sur Q : poids, tension). Figure du sujet extraite de la page numerisee sans filigrane (page 4) ; le texte parasite voisin a ete efface au recadrage.
9(ii) : la direction de la vitesse commune est donnee par rapport a la particule de 2 kg (sens positif choisi), le sujet ne fixant pas d'axe.

questions.enonce_markdown: (i)(a) Two particles $A$ and $B$ are moving in the plane of the coordinate axes $OX$ and $OY$. At time $t$ seconds, the position vectors of $A$ and $B$ are $(t^2\mathbf i+2\mathbf j)$ m and $(2\mathbf i-4t\mathbf j)$ m respectively. Calculate the distance between $A$ and $B$ when $t=2$. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
At $t=2$:

$\mathbf r_A=(2^2)\mathbf i+2\mathbf j=4\mathbf i+2\mathbf j,\qquad\mathbf r_B=2\mathbf i-8\mathbf j.$

$\overrightarrow{AB}=\mathbf r_B-\mathbf r_A=(2-4)\mathbf i+(-8-2)\mathbf j=-2\mathbf i-10\mathbf j.$

$|AB|=\sqrt{(-2)^2+(-10)^2}=\sqrt{104}=2\sqrt{26}\approx10.2.$

**The distance between $A$ and $B$ is $\sqrt{104}\approx10.2$ m.**

questions.enonce_markdown: (i)(b) With the same particles ($A$: $(t^2\mathbf i+2\mathbf j)$ m, $B$: $(2\mathbf i-4t\mathbf j)$ m), calculate the velocity of $A$ relative to $B$ when $t=2$. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Velocity is the derivative of the position vector:

$\mathbf v_A=\dfrac{d}{dt}(t^2\mathbf i+2\mathbf j)=2t\,\mathbf i,\qquad\mathbf v_B=\dfrac{d}{dt}(2\mathbf i-4t\mathbf j)=-4\mathbf j.$

At $t=2$: $\mathbf v_A=4\mathbf i$ and $\mathbf v_B=-4\mathbf j$.

Velocity of $A$ relative to $B$: $\mathbf v_{A/B}=\mathbf v_A-\mathbf v_B=4\mathbf i-(-4\mathbf j)=4\mathbf i+4\mathbf j.$

**$\mathbf v_{A/B}=(4\mathbf i+4\mathbf j)\ \text{m s}^{-1}$**, of magnitude $4\sqrt2\approx5.66\ \text{m s}^{-1}$, in the direction $45^\circ$ above $OX$.

questions.enonce_markdown: (ii)(a) Two particles, of masses 2 kg and 3 kg, are moving towards each other with speeds $6\ \text{m s}^{-1}$ and $2\ \text{m s}^{-1}$ respectively. After collision, they coalesce. Find their common velocity after collision. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Take the direction of motion of the 2 kg particle as positive. The 3 kg particle moves in the opposite direction, so its velocity is $-2$.

Conservation of momentum (the particles coalesce into one body of mass $5$ kg):

$2(6)+3(-2)=(2+3)v\ \Rightarrow\ 12-6=5v\ \Rightarrow\ v=\dfrac65=1.2.$

**The common velocity is $1.2\ \text{m s}^{-1}$**, in the direction in which the 2 kg particle was moving.

questions.enonce_markdown: (ii)(b) For the same collision (2 kg at $6\ \text{m s}^{-1}$ and 3 kg at $2\ \text{m s}^{-1}$, moving towards each other and coalescing), find the loss in kinetic energy due to the collision. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Kinetic energy before: $\dfrac12(2)(6)^2+\dfrac12(3)(2)^2=36+6=42$ J.

Kinetic energy after: $\dfrac12(5)(1.2)^2=\dfrac12(5)(1.44)=3.6$ J.

Loss $=42-3.6=38.4$ J.

**The loss in kinetic energy is $38.4$ J.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
(iii) ![fig-1](gce-ol-additional-maths-2025-p2-officiel-cameroun_exercice_9_fig_1.png)

A particle $P$ of mass 3 kg resting on a smooth horizontal table is connected by a light inextensible string passing over a smooth pulley to a particle $Q$ of mass $m$ kg hanging freely. The particles are released from rest with the string taut as shown in the diagram above and they move with an acceleration of $2\ \text{m s}^{-2}$.

(a) Draw a diagram showing all the forces acting on the particles. *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Forces on each particle (the string is light and the pulley smooth, so the tension $T$ is the same on both sides):

- **Particle $P$ (3 kg, on the table):** its weight $3g=30$ N acting **downwards**; the normal reaction $R$ of the table acting **upwards** ($R=30$ N, since $P$ does not move vertically); the tension $T$ in the string acting **horizontally** towards the pulley. There is no friction (smooth table).
- **Particle $Q$ ($m$ kg, hanging):** its weight $mg$ acting **downwards**; the tension $T$ in the string acting **upwards**.

Diagram (described): draw $P$ as a box on the horizontal table with arrows $R$ (up), $3g$ (down) and $T$ (to the right, towards the pulley); draw $Q$ as a box hanging from the string with arrows $T$ (up) and $mg$ (down). Label the acceleration $2\ \text{m s}^{-2}$ ($P$ moves towards the pulley, $Q$ moves down).

questions.enonce_markdown: (iii)(b) For the system of $P$ (3 kg on a smooth horizontal table) and $Q$ ($m$ kg hanging) joined by a light inextensible string over a smooth pulley, with acceleration $2\ \text{m s}^{-2}$, calculate the value of $m$. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Apply Newton's second law ($F=ma$) to each particle, taking the direction of motion as positive.

For $P$ (horizontal motion): $T=3\times2=6$ N. $\quad(1)$

For $Q$ (moving down): $mg-T=m\times2$, that is $10m-T=2m.\quad(2)$

Substitute $T=6$ into (2): $10m-6=2m\Rightarrow8m=6\Rightarrow m=0.75.$

Check: $mg-T=7.5-6=1.5=0.75\times2$.

**$m=0.75$ kg.**

questions.enonce_markdown: (iii)(c) For the same system, calculate the tension in the string. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
From the equation of motion of $P$: $T=3a=3\times2=6$ N.

Check with $Q$: $T=mg-ma=0.75(10)-0.75(2)=7.5-1.5=6$ N.

**The tension in the string is $6$ N.**
